camp-dubois:
Camp Dubois

Clark leads the party away from Camp Dubois and onto the Missouri. Lewis joins them later at St. Charles.

Location: Near the historic departure area; approximate.

Historical source — National Park Service
chinook-point:
Chinook Point

The party sees the Pacific near Chinook Point. Earlier, on November 7, Clark had mistaken the broad Columbia estuary for the ocean.

Location: Approximate viewpoint near Chinook Point.

Historical source — National Park Service
floyd:
Sergeant Floyd

Sergeant Charles Floyd dies near present-day Sioux City. He is the only expedition member to die during the journey.

Location: Modern monument area; approximate historical location.

Historical source — National Park Service
fort-clatsop:
Fort Clatsop

The party moves into Fort Clatsop during December. A wet coastal winter is spent preparing supplies, journals, and maps for the return.

Fort Clatsop replica. Image: National Park Service; this is a modern reconstruction.

Location: Modern reconstructed fort near the historical site.

Historical source — National Park Service
fort-mandan:
Fort Mandan

The party selects its winter quarters near Mandan and Hidatsa communities. Sacagawea and Toussaint Charbonneau join the expedition here.

Location: Approximate historic area, not the modern replica. The original fort location is uncertain.

Historical source — National Park Service
great-falls:
Great Falls

Lewis reaches the Great Falls of the Missouri. The sequence of falls forces the party to carry boats and supplies overland.

Location: General Great Falls area; the portage extended well beyond this marker.

Historical source — National Park Service
lemhi-pass:
Lemhi Pass

Lewis reaches Lemhi Pass. Mountain ranges beyond the divide challenge the hope of an easy water connection to the Pacific.

Location: Approximate pass location.

Historical source — National Park Service
st-louis:
St. Louis

The Corps returns to St. Louis after crossing the continent and back. Its journals and maps record the journey and the people encountered.

Location: Approximate riverfront arrival area.

Historical source — National Park Service
weippe:
Weippe Prairie

Clark’s advance party emerges from the Bitterroot Mountains at Weippe Prairie. Nez Perce hosts provide food and knowledge of the country.

Location: General prairie location, not an exact village site.

Historical source — National Park Service
